description: Synthetic rare-disease cases written for evaluation. Each is loosely modelled on the style of ZebraMap case reports (age, sex, presenting course, findings, tests) but written from scratch: no sentence is copied from ZebraMap or Orphanet. Gold labels are Orphanet IDs from the 1,464-disease retrieval catalog. Difficulty: typical = classic presentation; partial = fewer hallmark features and some noise; brief = one or two lines, as in a referral note.
author: synthetic, 2026-11-24

cases.text: A 41-year-old woman noticed blurred central vision in her right eye over two months. Since her twenties she has had soft yellowish bumps on the sides of the neck that look like plucked chicken skin, and lax skin folds in both armpits. Fundoscopy shows grey-brown streaks radiating from the optic disc in both eyes with a subretinal haemorrhage on the right. Skin biopsy shows fragmented, calcified elastic fibres in the mid-dermis.

A 23-year-old man has had episodes of burning pain in his hands and feet since childhood, worse with fever and exercise, and he hardly sweats. He has clusters of small dark red spots between the umbilicus and knees. Urine shows proteinuria and slit-lamp examination shows whorl-like corneal opacities. His maternal uncle had kidney failure and a stroke at 45.

A 16-year-old girl of Ashkenazi Jewish descent is referred for easy bruising and nosebleeds. She has a massively enlarged spleen and an enlarged liver, platelets of 62,000 and mild anaemia. She has had episodes of severe thigh bone pain, and MRI shows Erlenmeyer flask deformity of the distal femurs. Bone marrow aspirate shows large cells with wrinkled tissue-paper cytoplasm.

A 19-year-old man developed a tremor of both hands, slurred speech and drooling over six months, and his grades have dropped. Liver enzymes are mildly raised. Slit-lamp examination shows a golden-brown ring at the edge of the cornea. Serum ceruloplasmin is low and 24-hour urinary copper is markedly high.

A 17-year-old boy, 196 cm tall, is seen after his basketball coach noticed long arms and fingers. He has a pectus excavatum, arm span greater than height, positive wrist and thumb signs and flat feet. He is very short-sighted and the ophthalmologist found upward displacement of both lenses. Echocardiography shows dilatation of the aortic root. His father died suddenly in his thirties.

A 9-year-old girl has eight flat light-brown skin patches larger than 1.5 cm, freckling in both armpits and groins, and two soft skin nodules on her back. Slit-lamp examination shows small pigmented iris nodules. She has learning difficulties at school. Her mother has many soft lumps on her skin.

A 6-year-old boy with seizures since infancy, which started as clusters of spasms, and autism. He has several white leaf-shaped patches on his trunk, red papules across the nose and cheeks, and a rough leathery patch on his lower back. Brain MRI shows cortical tubers and subependymal nodules, and echocardiography in infancy showed cardiac rhabdomyomas.

A 3-year-old boy has had a high fever for six days that does not respond to antibiotics. He has red eyes without discharge, cracked red lips, a strawberry tongue, a widespread rash, swelling of the hands and feet and a single enlarged lymph node in the neck. The skin of his fingertips is starting to peel. Echocardiography shows dilated coronary arteries.

A 14-year-old girl of Armenian origin has had attacks of fever with severe abdominal pain lasting two to three days every few weeks since she was six. During attacks she has chest pain on breathing and occasionally a painful swollen ankle, and CRP is very high, returning to normal between attacks. An appendicectomy at 10 found no appendicitis. Her brother has similar attacks.

A 29-year-old woman has had daily spiking fevers above 39 degrees every evening for three weeks with a salmon-pink rash that appears with the fever and fades by morning. She has sore throat, painful wrists and knees, and enlarged lymph nodes. White cells are 21,000 with neutrophilia and ferritin is over 8,000. Blood cultures, ANA and rheumatoid factor are negative.

A 34-year-old woman complains of drooping eyelids and double vision that get worse towards the evening, and difficulty chewing at the end of meals. Her arms tire when she dries her hair. Symptoms improve after rest and with an ice pack on the eyelid. Repetitive nerve stimulation shows a decremental response and acetylcholine receptor antibodies are positive. CT chest shows an anterior mediastinal mass.

A 44-year-old man has developed irritability, depression and involuntary jerky, dance-like movements of his face and limbs over three years, and he has trouble planning at work. His walking is unsteady. His father had similar movements and died in a nursing home in his fifties. MRI shows atrophy of the caudate nuclei.

A 2-year-old girl who developed normally until 15 months has lost the few words she had and stopped using her hands purposefully. She now makes constant hand-wringing and hand-mouthing movements, has episodes of breath-holding and hyperventilation, and her head growth has slowed. She walks with a wide-based, stiff gait.

A 5-year-old boy was very floppy and fed poorly as a newborn, needing tube feeding. Since age three he has an insatiable appetite, steals food and is now obese. He has small hands and feet, almond-shaped eyes, undescended testes, short stature and temper tantrums, with mild learning disability.

A 14-year-old girl is referred for short stature and no breast development. She has a webbed neck, a low hairline at the back, a broad chest with widely spaced nipples and increased carrying angle at the elbows. She had swollen hands and feet at birth. Echocardiography shows a bicuspid aortic valve and LH and FSH are high.

A 17-year-old boy has not started puberty: no voice change, sparse body hair and small testes. He says he has never been able to smell anything. Testosterone, LH and FSH are all low, other pituitary hormones are normal and MRI shows absent olfactory bulbs.

A 48-year-old man notices his rings and shoes no longer fit and his jaw has become prominent, with gaps between his lower teeth. He snores heavily, sweats a lot, has carpal tunnel symptoms and new diabetes. IGF-1 is high and growth hormone does not suppress during a glucose tolerance test. MRI shows a pituitary macroadenoma.

A 32-year-old woman has had months of tiredness, weight loss, dizziness on standing and salt craving. Her skin has darkened, especially in palm creases, scars and gums. Blood pressure is 88/56 lying, sodium is low and potassium high. Morning cortisol is low with a very high ACTH and adrenal antibodies are positive.

A 38-year-old man has had nosebleeds several times a week since adolescence and now has iron-deficiency anaemia. He has small red spots on his lips, tongue and fingertips that blanch with pressure. CT chest shows a pulmonary arteriovenous malformation. His mother and sister also have frequent nosebleeds.

A 35-year-old woman has a dry cough and breathlessness for four months, with painful red lumps on her shins and swollen ankles. Chest X-ray shows enlarged lymph nodes at both lung hila. Serum ACE and calcium are raised. A lymph node biopsy shows non-caseating granulomas, and tests for tuberculosis are negative.

A 56-year-old man has bone pain in both legs and excessive thirst and urination. X-rays show symmetrical sclerosis of the long bones of the legs. CT shows soft tissue encasing both kidneys, giving a hairy kidney appearance, and thickening around the aorta. A biopsy contains foamy histiocytes that are CD68 positive and CD1a negative.

A 52-year-old man has had a blocked nose with bloody crusts and sinus pain for three months, then cough with blood-streaked sputum. His nasal bridge has started to collapse. CT chest shows several cavitating nodules, urine shows blood and red cell casts and creatinine is rising. c-ANCA with PR3 specificity is strongly positive.

A 47-year-old woman has difficulty climbing stairs and lifting her arms above her head over two months. She has a purple rash on her upper eyelids with swelling, scaly red bumps over her knuckles and a red rash on her upper chest and back. Creatine kinase is high and muscle biopsy shows perifascicular atrophy.

A 64-year-old man has deteriorated rapidly over three months, with memory loss, confusion, unsteady walking and visual disturbances. He now has sudden jerks of his limbs when startled. EEG shows periodic sharp wave complexes and MRI diffusion imaging shows ribbon-like signal in the cortex and basal ganglia. CSF 14-3-3 protein and RT-QuIC are positive.

A 31-year-old man notices dark brown urine in the morning that clears during the day, with tiredness and episodes of abdominal pain and difficulty swallowing. He has haemolytic anaemia with high LDH and a negative Coombs test. He recently had a clot in the hepatic veins. Flow cytometry shows loss of CD55 and CD59 on red cells.

A 28-year-old woman presents with confusion, fever and bruising after a week of headache. Platelets are 12,000, haemoglobin 7.8, the blood film shows fragmented red cells, LDH is very high and creatinine is mildly raised. Clotting tests are normal. ADAMTS13 activity is below 5 percent with an inhibitor.

A 22-year-old woman has had recurrent episodes of swelling of her hands, face and lips lasting two to four days since puberty, without hives or itch. She also has attacks of severe abdominal pain with vomiting. Antihistamines and steroids do not help. Her father had a throat swelling that needed an emergency tracheostomy. C4 is low and C1 inhibitor level and function are low.

A 52-year-old man has had back and knee pain for years. His urine turns black if left standing, which his mother noticed in his nappies. The whites of his eyes and his ear cartilage have bluish-black patches. X-rays show calcified intervertebral discs and he needed an aortic valve replacement. Urine homogentisic acid is very high.

A 4-year-old boy has had repeated chest infections with thick sputum, poor weight gain despite a large appetite, and bulky, greasy, foul-smelling stools. He had a bowel obstruction at birth. He has finger clubbing and nasal polyps. Sputum grows Pseudomonas and sweat chloride is 92 mmol/L on two occasions.

A 15-year-old boy has had blood in his urine since early childhood, now with protein in the urine and rising creatinine. He has progressive hearing loss for high tones and the ophthalmologist found anterior lenticonus and dot-and-fleck retinopathy. His maternal uncle needed a kidney transplant in his twenties. Kidney biopsy shows thinning and splitting of the glomerular basement membrane.

A 45-year-old woman has episodes of flushing, palpitations, abdominal cramps and diarrhoea, and she fainted after a wasp sting. She has small reddish-brown spots on her thighs that swell and itch when rubbed. Serum tryptase is persistently high, and bone marrow biopsy shows clusters of spindle-shaped mast cells with a KIT D816V mutation.

A 58-year-old farmer has lost 14 kg over a year with chronic diarrhoea and abdominal pain. For years before that he had flitting pain in large joints. He now has low-grade fever, enlarged lymph nodes and darkened skin. Duodenal biopsy shows villi stuffed with PAS-positive macrophages.

A 39-year-old woman has had difficulty swallowing both solids and liquids for two years, with regurgitation of undigested food at night, chest pain and weight loss. Barium swallow shows a dilated oesophagus narrowing to a bird's beak at the lower end. Manometry shows absent peristalsis and incomplete relaxation of the lower oesophageal sphincter.

A 7-year-old girl has had several brief episodes of weakness of one arm and slurred speech, often brought on by crying or blowing on hot food. She also has headaches. Angiography shows narrowing of both internal carotid artery ends with a network of fine collateral vessels at the base of the brain, like a puff of smoke.

A 61-year-old smoker has difficulty rising from a chair and climbing stairs, a dry mouth and constipation over three months. Reflexes are reduced but improve after brief exercise. Nerve conduction shows small muscle responses that increase markedly after exercise or high-frequency stimulation. Voltage-gated calcium channel antibodies are positive and CT shows a lung mass.

A 22-year-old man developed painless blurring of central vision in his left eye, followed six weeks later by the right eye. Visual acuity is now 6/60 in both eyes with central scotomas. The optic discs look swollen with small tortuous vessels but there is no leakage on angiography. His maternal uncle lost his sight at a similar age.

An 8-year-old boy has had eleven fractures after minor falls. He has blue-grey sclerae, short stature, bowing of the legs, loose joints and discoloured, translucent teeth. His mother also had many fractures as a child and became hard of hearing in her thirties. X-rays show thin bones with old healed fractures and wormian bones in the skull.

A 5-year-old girl has painful swellings on her neck and back that appeared after minor bumps and then became hard. She cannot turn her head well. Both big toes are short and bent inwards since birth. X-rays show bony bridges forming in the soft tissues of the back. A biopsy was considered but avoided.

A 46-year-old man has had repeated episodes of painful red swelling of both outer ears, sparing the earlobes, and red painful eyes. He has a hoarse voice and his nose bridge has started to sag. CT shows thickening of the trachea walls. Inflammatory markers are raised during attacks.

A 36-year-old woman presents with sudden right-sided chest pain and breathlessness from a pneumothorax, her second in two years. She has had increasing breathlessness on exertion. CT shows many thin-walled cysts throughout both lungs and a fatty kidney mass. Serum VEGF-D is raised.
Woman, 46. Loss of central vision; angioid streaks on fundoscopy; yellow papules on neck.
Teenager with tremor, abnormal liver tests and a corneal copper ring; low ceruloplasmin.
Fatigable ptosis and diplopia, worse in the evening. AChR antibodies positive.
Toddler, fever for 5 days, conjunctival injection, strawberry tongue, peeling fingers.
Severe thrombocytopenia, schistocytes, confusion, ADAMTS13 under 10 percent.
Child with multiple cafe-au-lait spots, axillary freckling and Lisch nodules.
